data.name: Rosaline
data.gender_notes: Rosaline is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'rosa', meaning 'rose'. Rosaline is a beautiful and elegant name with a rich history and a deep connection to the natural world. The name Rosaline carries the meaning “Little Rose” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Rosaline usually hope their child will grow to embody little rose and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Rosaline is a name that embodies the spiritual qualities of the rose, including love, beauty, and grace. It is a name that inspires us to connect with the natural world and to appreciate the beauty and wonder of creation.
data.etymology: Rosaline belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Little Rose.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rosaline total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rosaline has been cherished throughout history for its romantic and poetic associations. In medieval literature, it was common to find the name Rosaline or Rose™ used as a term of endearment, symbolizing love, beauty, and devotion. Today, the name retains a sense of classic charm and elegance, often capturing the imagination of those who hear it.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian faith, the rose often symbolizes the virtues of the Blessed Virgin Mary, representing her purity, grace, and mystical union with God. The name Rosaline can therefore be seen as a reminder of the spiritual journey, serving as a daily reminder to live in the presence of God and strive toward our own spiritual growth. Additionally, the name echoes the words of Saint Paul, who proclaimed, "I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me" (Galatians 2:20), suggesting that the true essence of our being is not found in ourselves, but in the divine love and grace of God. Thus, Rosaline can be seen as a powerful reminder of the transformative power of faith and love in our lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rosaline signifies the rosy hue of love's blush. It symbolizes the radiant beauty and deep devotion of one who embodies the divine spirit of love.
